title: Somatic cells kept their computational capacities and scaled them to anatomical goals

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Somatic cells kept their computational capacities and scaled them to anatomical goals

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Somatic cells did not lose the behavioural plasticity and computational capabilities of their unicellular ancestors when they became part of metazoan bodies; they scaled them to pursue larger goals, namely building and maintaining complex anatomies.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: somatic cells did not lose their behavioral plasticity and computational capabilities in becoming part of metazoan swarms (bodies): they scaled them to enable pursuit of larger goals consisting of creation and upkeep of massively complex anatomies (Pezzulo and Levin, 2015).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin”. Scope: Metazoan somatic cells compared with unicellular ancestors

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.37

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Comparative molecular and behavioral evidence can test retention of particular capacities, but not the broad claim that they were scaled to pursue anatomical goals as stated. Sparse taxonomic coverage and historical inference substantially limit discrimination.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare homologous sensing, signaling, learning-like response, and collective pattern-repair mechanisms across unicellular relatives and metazoan somatic cells, reconstructing whether capacities were retained and redeployed for organ-scale outcomes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Deep ancestral capacities cannot be directly observed.

Behavioral plasticity and larger goals have competing operationalizations.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Regulative development shows that somatic cells still produce target anatomies. That record is equally compatible with conserved computation, with new developmental gene networks, and with physiological feedback that nobody would call cognition. Nothing public distinguishes those readings, and the ancestral comparison cannot be measured. The claim stays conceptual.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Anatomical homeostasis after perturbation can be scored, but 'retained computational capacity' versus a later-evolved patterning mechanism uses the same regeneration outcomes. Ancestral unicellular behavior at the origin of metazoans is not a variable in any dataset.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The historical retention claim has no fossil or experimental record of the ancestor's computations.

Cognitive terms map onto ordinary regulative development.
